updates.title: GitHub adds client-level Copilot usage metrics
updates.whatChanged: On 23 October, GitHub added `totals_by_client` to Copilot usage reports for enterprise, organization, and user scopes. It reports model requests, sessions, prompt and output tokens, and client breakdowns in one-day and 28-day reports. The Copilot usage metrics policy must be enabled, and client IDs are best-effort.
updates.whyCare: You can compare Copilot model use across IDEs and external tools, then use request and token counts to guide support and governance. Client labels reflect integration IDs, so verify them against your own identity and endpoint telemetry.
updates.before: Reports showed usage by IDE but missed requests from tools without editor telemetry.
updates.after: Reports now group model requests, sessions, prompt tokens, output tokens, and client totals across one-day and 28-day views.
updates.learn: Enable the Copilot usage metrics policy. Compare client labels with your own telemetry before using them for attribution or governance.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - Usage metrics API adds usage from tools like OpenCode

updates.architectureImplication: Add `totals_by_client` to Copilot usage reviews. Treat the client value as a best-effort grouping and verify it against identity and endpoint telemetry before using it for policy decisions.
